observations: Photo 0: a white dry pressing iron standing on its heel on a tiled floor, with a temperature dial under the handle and no water tank or steam button.
The cloth-braided power cord is long and dirty, with at least one taped or patched join and frayed braiding near the iron end and near the plug.
One spot near the left of the cord shows coloured inner wires through a damaged section, likely a splice.
The three-pin plug is present; its cord entry looks frayed.
Body is scuffed and grimy; no brand name or label is readable.
The soleplate is not shown, and the iron is not shown plugged in or heating.

read_from: photo 0 iron body, temperature dial and corded design

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows a used dry iron with a temperature dial and no steam tank.
Photo 0 does not show it plugged in, the indicator light on, or it heating; priced as not working.
Location cannot be shown by the photo.

risks.risk: Iron does not heat, or the thermostat does not cut off
risks.proof: A clip of the iron plugged in with the light on, then pressing a damp cloth until it steams, and the light cycling off

risks.risk: Damaged and spliced power cord is a shock or fire hazard
risks.proof: Close-ups along the whole cord, the taped join and the plug entry

risks.risk: Soleplate scorched, scratched or with melted residue
risks.proof: Photo of the soleplate face in daylight
Photos of both sides and the back of the iron

proof_requests: Clip of the iron plugged in, light on, heating and pressing a cloth
Close-ups of the taped and frayed parts of the cord and the plug
Photos of both sides showing any brand label
response.reason: The photo clearly shows a used dry pressing iron, priced by type. With a visibly damaged, spliced cord and no proof of heating, it is priced as not working and needing a new cord.
